processing: A partly oxidised Guangdong oolong; the specifics of its making are not widely recorded.
harvest_season: Not well recorded; as with most Guangdong oolongs, spring is usually the most valued picking.
appearance_wet: Typical of oolong: leaves that open fully; the name suggests a large leaf.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record is widely available; Guangdong oolongs in general show natural floral and fruity sweetness.

brewing.notes: General oolong settings; adjust after the first steep.

vintage_note: Nothing specific is recorded about its sale. Usual for this class is the current year's harvest, drunk fresh, so ask for the year and season.
description:
Da Ye Qi Lan, big-leaf Qi Lan, is an oolong from Xingning in Guangdong, part of the modern group of Guangdong teas that grew up alongside the better-known Dancong.

What is on record is brief: sandy green, glossy dry leaf and a bright orange-yellow cup. Beyond that you are left with what is typical of Guangdong oolong, which is natural floral and fruity sweetness.

The name Qi Lan also belongs to a Fujian variety grown in Wuyi and elsewhere. Whether the Xingning plant is related is not established, so do not assume a Fujian Qi Lan and this tea are the same thing.

Brew it hot and short, and taste before you decide how far to push the steeps. It is rarely seen outside the region, so a seller's knowledge of the maker counts for a lot.
history: The tea is dated to the 1980s, placing it among the Guangdong oolongs developed in the same period as Lingtou Dancong and Xi Yan Wulong. No maker or institution is commonly named for it.
